title: How are you supposed to read the Bible in context?
hook_0_2s: You are reading the Bible completely wrong.

segments.text: You are reading the Bible completely wrong. Most of us open it looking for a quick fix to today's problem. But in first-century Jerusalem, Scripture was never read as isolated fortune cookies. It was read aloud as one unified story leading to Jesus.

In John chapter 5, verse 39, Jesus looked at the religious scholars on the Temple steps and said: You search the Scriptures because you think they give you eternal life, yet they are the very words that testify about Me.

When you pull a single verse out of its chapter, you lose the entire weight of what God is actually doing. So tonight, before you ask what does this verse fix for me, ask what does this chapter reveal about Him. Because until you shift that lens...

loop_bridge: ...Because until you shift that lens... -> You are reading the Bible completely wrong.
keywords: how to read the bible in context
pinned_comment: Which Bible verse did you grow up hearing quoted completely out of context?

title: What does the word meek actually mean in the Bible?
hook_0_2s: The word meek in the Bible does not mean weak.

segments.text: The word meek in the Bible does not mean weak. Modern culture hears meekness and pictures someone fragile, passive, or easily pushed around. That is the exact opposite of what Jesus said on the mountainside.

When Jesus said in Matthew chapter 5, verse 5, Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth, the Greek word He used was praus—the military term for a warhorse trained to hold steady in battle, or a sword rested inside its sheath.

Biblical meekness is not the absence of strength; it is absolute strength held under God's command. When you refuse to retaliate in anger today, you are not losing ground—you are keeping your blade sheathed. And that is why...

loop_bridge: ...And that is why... -> The word meek in the Bible does not mean weak.
keywords: what does meek mean in the bible
pinned_comment: Did you grow up thinking 'meek' meant weak or quiet? What changed how you read Matthew 5:5?

title: What was Jeremiah 29:11 actually written to say?
hook_0_2s: Jeremiah 29:11 was not written as a quick comfort verse.

segments.text: Jeremiah 29:11 was not written as a quick comfort verse. We print it on coffee mugs as if God promises an instant escape from every hard season. Look at the verses right above it.

Jeremiah was writing to exiles in Babylon after telling them they would stay in captivity for seventy years. Build houses and settle down, the Lord said, for I know the plans I have for you—plans to give you a future and a hope.

God did not promise to pull them out of the fire tomorrow; He promised to sustain them inside the waiting. If your prayer hasn't been answered yet, your exile is not a sign that God forgot you. And that is the real reason...

loop_bridge: ...And that is the real reason... -> Jeremiah 29:11 was not written as a quick comfort verse.
pinned_comment: Where is the most unexpected place you've seen Jeremiah 29:11 printed—and how does knowing the 70-year context change it for you?
